page: Amazon Web Services c8gb.24xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by 96 dedicated physical cores of the ARMv9 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor. Operating at 2.8 GHz on the arm64 architecture, it features 192.0 GB of memory, translating to 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache. This instance runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data reveals top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU and Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 11075.0 GB/sec for cached read-only small blocks and 480.77 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Multi-threaded operations, such as bzip3 decompression and software compilation with Clang, also rank in the top 10%. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling in the middle 50%.

The instance provides a high baseline network bandwidth of 200 Gbps. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high physical core density and dedicated ARMv9 architecture offer strong resource density for parallel workloads without hyperthreading overhead. It is highly suited for multi-threaded workloads, static web serving, database operations, software compilation, and medium-to-large LLM text generation tasks, while being less optimal for single-threaded or GPU-dependent applications.
